'''''Osmanthus heterophyllus''''' ([[Chinese language|Chinese]]:<small>[[traditional characters|t]]</small> {{lang|zh|{{linktext|柊樹}}}}, <small>[[simplified characters|s]]</small> {{lang|zh|{{linktext|柊树}}}}, <small>[[pinyin|p]]</small> ''zhōngshù''; {{langx|ja|{{linktext|柊}}}}, ''hiiragi''), variously known as '''holly osmanthus''', '''holly olive''', and '''false holly''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the olive [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Oleaceae, [[native plant|native]] to eastern Asia in central and southern Japan ([[Honshū]], [[Kyūshū]], [[Shikoku]], and the [[Ryukyu Islands]]) and Taiwan.<ref name=foc>Flora of China: [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=210001396 ''Osmanthus heterophyllus'']</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 2 January 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to {{convert|2|-|8|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall. The [[Bark (botany)|bark]] is brown to grey or blackish, cracking into small plates on old plants. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, 3–7 cm long and 1.5–4 cm broad with a thick, leathery texture, lustrous dark green above, paler yellow-green below; the margin is entire or with one to four large spine-tipped teeth on each side. Spiny leaves predominate on small, young plants (an adaptation to deter browsing animals), while entire leaves predominate higher on larger mature plants out of the reach of animals. The [[flower]]s are very fragrant, white, with a four-lobed [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]], the corolla tube 1–2 mm long and the lobes 2.5–5 mm long; they are [[dioecy|dioecious]], with flowering in the autumn. The [[fruit]] is an ovoid dark purple [[drupe]] 1.5 cm long and 1 cm diameter, mature in the following summer about 9 months after flowering.<ref name=foc/><ref name=hl>Hata Labs Plant Ecology Laboratory: [http://had0.big.ous.ac.jp/plantsdic/angiospermae/dicotyledoneae/sympetalae/oleaceae/hiiragi/hiiragi.htm ''Osmanthus heterophyllus''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806021117/http://had0.big.ous.ac.jp/plantsdic/angiospermae/dicotyledoneae/sympetalae/oleaceae/hiiragi/hiiragi.htm |date=2020-08-06 }} (in Japanese; [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=http://had0.big.ous.ac.jp/plantsdic/angiospermae/dicotyledoneae/sympetalae/oleaceae/hiiragi/hiiragi.htm&sa=X&oi=translate& google translation])</ref><ref name=rmg>Rokko Mountain guide to trees: [http://shinrin.cool.ne.jp/sub222.html ''Osmanthus heterophyllus''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050525144033/http://shinrin.cool.ne.jp/sub222.html |date=2005-05-25 }} (in Japanese; [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=http://shinrin.cool.ne.jp/sub222.html&sa=X&oi=translate& google translation])</ref><ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref>

==Varieties==
There are two [[variety (botany)|varieties]]:<ref name=foc/>
*''Osmanthus heterophyllus'' var. ''heterophyllus''. Leaves entire or spiny; flowers with short corolla lobes 2.5-3.5 mm long. Throughout the range of the species.
*''Osmanthus heterophyllus'' var. ''bibracteatus'' (Hayata) P.S.Green. Leaves always entire; flowers with long corolla lobes 5 mm long. Endemic to Taiwan.

==Nomenclature==
''Osmanthus'' is derived from [[Greek language|Greek]] and means 'fragrant flower'.<ref name= "gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 285, 410</ref>

The scientific name ''heterophyllus'', "different leaves", refers to the variation in leaf shape between spiny and entire. The common name holly osmanthus refers to the similarity in leaf shape to that of the [[Ilex aquifolium|holly]] (''Ilex aquifolium''), an example of [[convergent evolution]] with a common objective of deterring browsing; the two may be distinguished easily by the leaf arrangement, alternate in ''Ilex aquifolium'' and opposite in ''Osmanthus heterophyllus''.

==Cultivation==
[[File:Goshiki False Holly plants growing in New Jersey in April.jpg|thumb|right|‘Goshiki’, [[Cranford, New Jersey]]]]
It is widely used as a [[Hedge (barrier)|hedge]] plant.<ref name=rhs/><ref name="themagicholly">{{cite journal |last=Sakanishi |first=Shio |date=December 1935|title=The Magic Holly in Japanese Literature |journal=[[Journal of the American Oriental Society]] |volume=55 |issue=4 |pages=444–450|doi=10.2307/594762 |jstor=594762}}</ref> Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected for garden use, including 'Aureus', 'Goshiki', 'Purpureus', 'Rotundifolius', and 'Subangustatus'.<ref name=rhs/> The cultivars 'Goshiki',<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Osmanthus heterophyllus'' 'Goshiki'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/116640/Osmanthus-heterophyllus-Goshiki-(v)/Details|access-date=14 September 2019}}</ref> 'Variegatus'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Osmanthus heterophyllus'' 'Variegatus'|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1358|access-date=25 May 2013}}{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and ‘Purple Shaft’ have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = 2018 
| page = 71 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 September 2019}}</ref>

The species has been hybridised in cultivation with ''[[Osmanthus fragrans]]''; the resulting [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] is named [[Osmanthus × fortunei|''Osmanthus'' × ''fortunei'']] <small>Carr</small>.<ref name=rhs/>

==Historical mentions==
It is mentioned twice in the ''[[Kojiki]]'', the oldest surviving historical record of Japan.<ref name="themagicholly"/> The first mention, under the name ''hihiragi'', is in connection with the name of a [[kami]], ''Hihiragi-no-sono-hana-madzumi-no-kami''<ref>{{cite book|title=[[Kojiki]]| pages = vol. 2, sect. 26}}</ref> (translated by [[Basil Hall Chamberlain|Chamberlain]] as "''Deity Waiting-to-see-the-Flowers-of-the-Holly''"<ref>{{cite book|last =Chamberlain|first=Basil Hall| author-link = Basil Hall Chamberlain|title=Kojiki|url =https://archive.org/details/kojikirecordsanc00cham|url-access =limited| pages = [https://archive.org/details/kojikirecordsanc00cham/page/n99 100]|year=1932|edition=2nd}}</ref>), with the word ''madzumi'' (''rarely seen'') being used to describe the plant's characteristic of its flowers rarely blossoming, as interpreted by the scholar Tominobu.<ref name="themagicholly"/><ref>{{cite book|last =Hosoda|first=Tominobu|title=Jindai seigo tokiwa-gusa}}</ref> Its second mention occurs during a passage referring to how a holly wood spear, made of material from the tree and spanning "eight fathoms long",<ref>{{cite book|last =Chamberlain|first=Basil Hall| author-link = Basil Hall Chamberlain|title=Kojiki|url =https://archive.org/details/kojikirecordsanc00cham|url-access =limited| pages = [https://archive.org/details/kojikirecordsanc00cham/page/n60 22]|year=1932|edition=2nd}}</ref> was presented to the Prince [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato-take]] by the Emperor prior to him being sent to subdue the East.<ref name="themagicholly"/> Its prickly and non-prickly variations are sometimes described as "male" and "female" respectively, though this does not have a relation to the plant's [[plant sexuality|gender]].<ref name="themagicholly"/><ref>{{cite book|last =Matsuoka|first=Gentatsu|title=Honzo ikka gen|year= c. 1800}}</ref>
